frequency_question: How often does an industrial base establish a new functional assembly line for a complex cruise missile within a 2-month timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state establishing a domestic assembly/production line for a foreign-designed cruise missile or precision-guided munition from scratch during wartime. Excludes routine facility upgrades or simple maintenance depots.

cases.name: US hurried cruise missile/drone production adjustments

provenance_note: claimed 0 hits but 1 of 3 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 3 named; universe of rapid sovereign cruise missile line setups is extremely sparse.
known_gaps: Classified defense industrial projects in other nations (e.g., Iran, North Korea) lack public timelines of sufficient granularity.
skeleton: Emergency missile facility establishment attempts divided by total attempts within accelerated wartime windows of less than 3 months.
multiplier: 0 hits out of 3 major accelerated complex-guidance assembly setups completed successfully within a sub-quarter timeline.
validity_reason: Advanced manufacturing speeds (like 3D printing and modular robotics) evolve slowly relative to the massive physical lead times of aerospace tooling.
